assertion.statement: For the fixed modular curve and fixed phi, finitely many cusp differences have finite image subgroup killed by one fixed C_pi.
assertion.objects: The fixed X0(N), its finite set of cusps, J0(N), and fixed homomorphism phi:J0(N)->E.
assertion.hypotheses: The published cuspidal torsion theorem applies to the congruence curve; phi is a group homomorphism.
assertion.quantifiers: All cusp differences for this fixed curve and their images under phi.
assertion.parameter_range: Fixed level N; geometric cusps need not be rational.
assertion.uniformity: One exponent for the subgroup generated by this finite set.
assertion.constants: Existence of a positive exponent C_pi is concluded, not assumed.
assertion.normalizations: Degree-zero classes [c]-[infinity], then their images under phi.
assertion.exceptional_cases: No W eigen-action, formula or exponent over varying levels is supplied.
assertion.limit_order: Apply torsion to the finite generating cusp set, then take the finite image subgroup and an exponent.

assertion.statement: For an abelian variety over a characteristic-zero field, rational matrix units give abelian image factors over that same field, mutually isogenous via off-diagonal units; complementary images sum by an isogeny.
assertion.objects: The original A/L with its L-defined M2(k) action, diagonal idempotents e11,e22 and a common positive integer denominator m.
assertion.hypotheses: The idempotents and matrix units belong to End_L^0(A); the image construction uses properness, geometric connectedness, and smoothness of finite-type group schemes in characteristic zero (the retained Cartier input).
assertion.quantifiers: Every rational matrix-unit system on this same abelian variety and every common denominator clearing it.
assertion.parameter_range: Characteristic zero; here dim A=2 and the two matrix-unit factors have equal positive dimension.
assertion.uniformity: All images and maps are defined over L; no further field extension is introduced.
assertion.constants: Choose any positive integer m clearing the matrix-unit denominators; no uniform isogeny-degree bound is asserted by this algebraic construction.
assertion.normalizations: X_i=image(m e_ii); addition p and tuple q satisfy pq=[m] and qp=[m]. Off-diagonal units provide rational isomorphisms between X_i, and End^0(X_i)=e_ii End^0(A)e_ii.
assertion.exceptional_cases: Images do not depend on the chosen denominator. This is not a polarization-preserving isogeny assertion and does not give a good-reduction field bound or a quantitative isogeny estimate.
assertion.limit_order: First obtain L-defined full endomorphisms; then clear denominators, construct the images, and use the matrix-unit identities. Dimension two gives elliptic factors; the corner k gives CM.

available_assertion.hypotheses: The idempotents and matrix units belong to End_L^0(A); the image construction uses properness, geometric connectedness, and smoothness of finite-type group schemes in characteristic zero (the retained Cartier input).
available_assertion.quantifiers: Every rational matrix-unit system on this same abelian variety and every common denominator clearing it.
available_assertion.parameter_range: Characteristic zero; here dim A=2 and the two matrix-unit factors have equal positive dimension.
available_assertion.uniformity: All images and maps are defined over L; no further field extension is introduced.
available_assertion.constants: Choose any positive integer m clearing the matrix-unit denominators; no uniform isogeny-degree bound is asserted by this algebraic construction.
available_assertion.normalizations: X_i=image(m e_ii); addition p and tuple q satisfy pq=[m] and qp=[m]. Off-diagonal units provide rational isomorphisms between X_i, and End^0(X_i)=e_ii End^0(A)e_ii.
available_assertion.exceptional_cases: Images do not depend on the chosen denominator. This is not a polarization-preserving isogeny assertion and does not give a good-reduction field bound or a quantitative isogeny estimate.
available_assertion.limit_order: First obtain L-defined full endomorphisms; then clear denominators, construct the images, and use the matrix-unit identities. Dimension two gives elliptic factors; the corner k gives CM.

assertion.hypotheses: v(p)=1, integral model and unit D; Q is already formal and nonidentity; P has infinite order. The reduction-order and CRT construction supplying d is separate.
assertion.quantifiers: Every indicated primary completion and actual Q satisfying these hypotheses.
assertion.parameter_range: Depth r>=1>1/(p-1), multiplication by the integer p^19.
assertion.uniformity: Exact isometry and equality of valuations; no asymptotic constant or assumption about another completion.
assertion.constants: Depth increase exactly19 and resulting lower bound20.
assertion.normalizations: z=-x/y and normalized additive formal logarithm with linear coefficient1.
assertion.exceptional_cases: Do not apply the logarithm before Q is formal. Nonidentity follows from the separate infinite-order premise and nonzero integer multiplier. No conclusion about opposite-place depths without their own congruences.
assertion.limit_order: Reduction-order congruences first put Q in the formal subgroup; use log([p^19]Q)=p^19 log(Q), then isometry at both formal points. Tail-error estimates are subsequent distinct inputs.

assertion.limit_order: Isolate binomial digit, prove parity/inclusion, then disjointness and AND before applying masks.

assertion.statement: For genuine isogenies of abelian surfaces, degree is multiplicative and deg([n])=n^4 for nonzero integers n.
assertion.objects: Integral denominator-cleared isogenies [m]u and their compositions with multiplication maps on abelian surfaces.
assertion.hypotheses: Characteristic zero; m,n are positive integers for which the representatives are genuine isogenies.
assertion.quantifiers: Every such integral representative and positive m,n.
assertion.parameter_range: Genuine integral isogenies only; rational quasi-isogeny degree is subsequently defined and proved well-defined.
assertion.uniformity: The same degree law holds independently of coefficient prime and is unchanged by field conjugation.
assertion.constants: deg([n]([m]u))=n^4 deg([m]u).
assertion.normalizations: Degree is the rank of the finite locally free map; [-1] is a degree-one automorphism.
assertion.exceptional_cases: No degree assigned to [1/m] as an algebraic morphism; no rational discrepancy or finite cochain conclusion in this source input.
assertion.limit_order: Apply the integral theorem before dividing numerical degrees by m^4.

assertion.statement: The original b caller's V_5(A) admits the nondegenerate alternating G_F-equivariant pairing into Q_5(1) used in the determinant calculation.
assertion.objects: The same abelian surface A over the finite number field F of actual Tate restriction, and an F-defined polarization lambda:A->A^dual.
assertion.hypotheses: A is an abelian variety over F of characteristic zero. Choose an ample F-line bundle and its polarization; retain the original normalized-family Tate restriction separately.
assertion.quantifiers: For all x,y in V_5(A) and g in G_F, the pairing satisfies <gx,gy>=epsilon_5(g)<x,y>.
assertion.parameter_range: ell=5; no condition on reduction at 5 or on the 5-part of deg(lambda).
assertion.uniformity: The construction applies to this original A and F; it asserts no uniform field degree and makes no replacement of the family.
assertion.constants: Multiplier epsilon_5. Nondegeneracy is over Q_5, regardless of the integral cokernel of T_5(lambda).
assertion.normalizations: Covariant Tate modules and the roots-of-unity Tate twist Q_5(1). The dual pairing is composed in the second factor with lambda.
assertion.exceptional_cases: A principal polarization and degree prime to 5 are unnecessary. Skew symmetry is alternating in characteristic zero. Pairing supply does not establish the separate two-copy identity.
assertion.limit_order: Take compatible prime-power torsion pairings, pass to Tate modules, tensor with Q_5, and compose with the isogeny lambda.

assertion.statement: Obtain the Gaussian fixed-field weighted Hecke prime estimate uniformly in rational progression moduli q<=log(X)^B.
assertion.objects: E=Q(i); fixed finite-order ray character chi of modulus m; rational Dirichlet rho modulo q; theta(a)=chi(a)rho(Na), a ray character modulo m(q), whose finite modulus norm is at most Nm*q^2.
assertion.hypotheses: For q<=(log X)^B and sqrtX<=Y<=X, Nm*q^2<=(log Y)^(2B+1) for sufficiently large X depending only on m,B. Mitsui applies with fixed K=E and A=2B+1, uniformly over rho,q. SmallY<sqrtX handled by elementary ideal von Mangoldt sum bound. Fixed bounded X absorbed. Principal indicator checked by inducing character.
assertion.quantifiers: For every choice of the application parameters satisfying these hypotheses at the named current consumer; no conclusion is claimed for a different proof stage.
assertion.parameter_range: For q<=(log X)^B and sqrtX<=Y<=X, Nm*q^2<=(log Y)^(2B+1) for sufficiently large X depending only on m,B. Mitsui applies with fixed K=E and A=2B+1, uniformly over rho,q. SmallY<sqrtX handled by elementary ideal von Mangoldt sum bound. Fixed bounded X absorbed. Principal indicator checked by inducing character.
assertion.uniformity: Subtract the smoothed prime sums at x*exp(h) and x to prove unsmoothing for complex characters; bound prime powers of exponent>=2 by O_E(sqrtY log^2(2Y)); replace error atY by Xexp(-c sqrtlogX). Optional primitive-to-imprimitive restoration costs O_chi(log(q+2)log(Y+2)). Any fixed log-power saving follows. No extra Fogels external application is consumed by this proof.
assertion.constants: For a fixed number field and finite-order ray characters of logarithmically bounded modulus norm, the weighted prime-ideal sum has main term X exactly for the character induced from the trivial primitive character and error X exp(-c sqrt(log X)), uniformly in the permitted characters and moduli, with ineffective fixed-data constants.
assertion.normalizations: Normalized ideal norm; Lambda_K(p^j)=log Np for j>=1; finite-order ray characters extended by zero at excluded primes; all residue degrees included; principal means induced by the trivial primitive character. Fixed field and logarithmic exponent. Constants ineffective.
assertion.exceptional_cases: Complex characters require the explicit unsmoothing; prime powers and omitted Euler factors are removed separately.
assertion.limit_order: Fix the Gaussian ray data and B; use the conductor norm bound for sqrt(X)<=Y<=X, then treat short Y separately.

assertion.statement: For Q_kappa in five variables obtain the uniform nonprimitive count needed before the displayed Mobius inversion.
assertion.objects: The five-variable nondegenerate isotropic Q_kappa, kappa!=0, nonnegative smooth weight away from zero, and arbitrary nonempty sets of nonzero good-modulus quadric residues.
assertion.hypotheses: n=5 is permitted (n≥5, not n>5). Qκ has κ≠0, rank5 and rational isotropic point (1,0,1,0,0). Modulus squarefree, coprime to2κ, hence to2ΔQ; each residue subset is in nonzero zeros. Smooth compact support away from origin, so gradient bounded away from0. Error B^(n/2+ε)m^(n/2+ε) uniform in modulus/subsets; derivatives may depend on fixedτ. The weight is nonnegative; empty allowed sets are handled by the zero count.
assertion.quantifiers: For every choice of the application parameters satisfying these hypotheses at the named current consumer; no conclusion is claimed for a different proof stage.
assertion.parameter_range: n=5 is permitted (n≥5, not n>5). Qκ has κ≠0, rank5 and rational isotropic point (1,0,1,0,0). Modulus squarefree, coprime to2κ, hence to2ΔQ; each residue subset is in nonzero zeros. Smooth compact support away from origin, so gradient bounded away from0. Error B^(n/2+ε)m^(n/2+ε) uniform in modulus/subsets; derivatives may depend on fixedτ. The weight is nonnegative; empty allowed sets are handled by the zero count.
assertion.uniformity: Rescale by h in Möbius sum. For (h,m)=1, h^-1Ω has same size; otherwise no contribution. Sum errors absolutely and calculate local densities.
assertion.constants: For an isotropic nondegenerate integral quadratic form F in n>=5 variables and a nonnegative smooth compactly supported weight away from the gradient-zero locus, the weighted count of all integral zeros satisfying nonempty admissible sets of local zeros that are nonzero modulo each relevant prime has the product-density main term and error O_(epsilon,F,w)(B^(n/2+epsilon) M^(n/2+epsilon)), uniformly in M and allowed subsets when M is coprime to twice the discriminant.
assertion.normalizations: BL counts all integral zeros; appendix imposes global primitivity by Möbius inversion. Hessian/determinant discriminant conventions differ only by powers of2 here. Primitive local density is1−p^-4; conditioning denominator p^4−1.
assertion.exceptional_cases: Empty local sets contribute zero; n=5 is allowed. Primitive normalization is obtained by the separate Mobius sum.
assertion.limit_order: Fix kappa, the smooth nonnegative weight and tau before varying B and the admissible squarefree modulus.

assertion.hypotheses: Base field Q(i), maximal order Z[i], finite nonzero modulusHZ[i], no real places. Class number1 gives ray quotient of residue units by four Gaussian units. Stable modulus under conjugation gives ray extension Galois overQ. H0 divisible16 makes unit embedding injective; added primes avoid2H0.
assertion.quantifiers: For every choice of the application parameters satisfying these hypotheses at the named current consumer; no conclusion is claimed for a different proof stage.

assertion.uniformity: Derive exact kernel∏Bℓ, commutators∏kerNorm, abelian quotient, and surviving norm-fibre proportions at least1−4/(ℓ−1). The product quotient is established by the unramified-intersection and degree argument, not by trivial conjugation alone.
assertion.constants: The published ray-class existence, exact sequence and reciprocity theorems identify the ray class field and its Artin map. For the maximal Gaussian order with no real places, the residue-unit quotient by global units gives the ray group, with arithmetic Frobenius convention.

assertion.limit_order: Fix the base modulus H_0 and then adjoin the stated new primes, retaining all ramification exclusions.

assertion.statement: Extend g to the real polynomial orbit and compose with (t-b)/W in the same filtered polynomial class.
assertion.objects: Extend the coordinate polynomials of g(n) to real t, form g_R(t), then tilde-g(t)=g_R((t-b)/W).
assertion.hypotheses: W>=1 and b are fixed integers, 0<=b<W. Affine composition preserves every coordinate degree constraint for the original filtration; real exponential coordinates exist in connected simply connected nilpotent G.
assertion.quantifiers: For every choice of the application parameters satisfying these hypotheses at the named current consumer; no conclusion is claimed for a different proof stage.
assertion.parameter_range: W>=1 and b are fixed integers, 0<=b<W. Affine composition preserves every coordinate degree constraint for the original filtration; real exponential coordinates exist in connected simply connected nilpotent G.
assertion.uniformity: tilde-g is a polynomial sequence on the same nilmanifold and tilde-g(Wn+b)=g(n). This is an algebraic interpolation statement, not assumed fractional-argument equidistribution.
assertion.constants: The one-parameter coordinate characterization allows polynomial extension of the Malcev coordinates to real arguments; affine precomposition preserves their filtration degree constraints.
assertion.normalizations: G connected, simply connected and nilpotent; Gamma discrete cocompact; filtration by closed connected rational subgroups; adapted rational Malcev basis; C-infinity norm in the binomial basis modulo one; Lipschitz norm includes supremum norm. Nontrivial horizontal characters are integer-lattice characters annihilating commutators and Gamma.
assertion.exceptional_cases: Polynomial real extension supplies the fractional argument; no distribution assertion at fractional points is assumed.
assertion.limit_order: Fix integer W and b before the large orbit scale.

assertion.statement: Obtain the normalized majorant mean on fixed-relative-length intervals required by the boundary cutoff.
assertion.objects: Take one affine divisor-sum factor W*x+b and a fixed relative-length interval I in the enlarged ambient domain; nu0=1 is immediate if no anchor is present.
assertion.hypotheses: Freeze v and epsilon before the size limit. b is a unit modulo W, the smooth cutoff is fixed and the sieve exponent is sufficiently small. Singleton convex-body specialization has no pairwise degeneracy condition to check. Use the same cutoff normalization as in nu0; its total-mass normalization is one. At primes dividing W, normalization cancels the unit local factor.
assertion.quantifiers: For every choice of the application parameters satisfying these hypotheses at the named current consumer; no conclusion is claimed for a different proof stage.
assertion.parameter_range: Freeze v and epsilon before the size limit. b is a unit modulo W, the smooth cutoff is fixed and the sieve exponent is sufficiently small. Singleton convex-body specialization has no pairwise degeneracy condition to check. Use the same cutoff normalization as in nu0; its total-mass normalization is one. At primes dividing W, normalization cancels the unit local factor.
assertion.uniformity: Obtain E1_I*nu0=|I|/n plus the stated iterated errors. Together with weighted L2 this gives O(epsilon)+cutoff error+size error for boundary strips.
assertion.constants: The normalized divisor-sum convex-body estimate gives the mean of a single unit-residue affine majorant over a fixed relative-length interval, with the stated iterated cutoff and size errors. This is a singleton specialization of the source estimate.
assertion.normalizations: This is a specialization of a proved divisor-sum/convex-body estimate, not a separately named interval-prime theorem. No claim that global L1 or global Gowers smallness alone implies the interval mean.
assertion.exceptional_cases: Global L1 normalization alone is insufficient; use the one-form convex-domain divisor-sum estimate.
assertion.limit_order: Freeze v and epsilon before size; only then pass to the outer cutoff limit.

available_assertion.statement: The Green-Tao divisor-sum construction provides a nonnegative normalized prime-cyclic majorant with any requested fixed finite pseudorandom complexity and domination of the appropriately rescaled prime weight, under its stated cutoff and size hypotheses.
available_assertion.objects: Prime-cyclic divisor-sum majorant for the ordinary prime weight.
available_assertion.hypotheses: A requested fixed finite pseudorandom complexity and the source construction cutoff/size hypotheses; use unit residue classes for the W-tricked weight.
available_assertion.quantifiers: For every source object and parameter choice meeting the explicitly stated hypotheses.
available_assertion.parameter_range: Prime cyclic ambient size comparable to the interval, sufficiently large for fixed complexity.
available_assertion.uniformity: Domination and pseudorandom estimates under the specified fixed-parameter hypotheses.
available_assertion.normalizations: Nonnegative majorant normalized to asymptotic mean one, with full linear-forms and correlation conditions.
available_assertion.exceptional_cases: The published construction does not itself specify the current fixed-E averaging, nu=(1+tilde-nu)/2, or gamma=1/(32S); these are current derivations.
available_assertion.limit_order: Fix complexity and construction parameters before size, respecting the source cutoff conditions.
available_assertion.constants: The Green-Tao divisor-sum construction provides a nonnegative normalized prime-cyclic majorant with any requested fixed finite pseudorandom complexity and domination of the appropriately rescaled prime weight, under its stated cutoff and size hypotheses.

needed_assertion.statement: Supply the full linear-forms and correlation majorant input, with fixed modulus factor E and unit residues, at every complexity requested by the current relative inverse step.
needed_assertion.objects: Fixed E,T,S,C_*; V=E product_(p<=z)p; unit residues b_i; prime Q in [C_*L,2C_*L]; the explicit smoothed divisor-square measure.
needed_assertion.hypotheses: S covers every required linear-forms and correlation order, in particular (k+2)2^(k+1) for the target U^(k+1) relative inverse theorem; z<=log log log L grows sufficiently slowly. Both pseudorandomness conditions are required.
needed_assertion.quantifiers: For every choice of the application parameters satisfying these hypotheses at the named current consumer; no conclusion is claimed for a different proof stage.
needed_assertion.parameter_range: S covers every required linear-forms and correlation order, in particular (k+2)2^(k+1) for the target U^(k+1) relative inverse theorem; z<=log log log L grows sufficiently slowly. Both pseudorandomness conditions are required.
needed_assertion.uniformity: Uniform in all stated unit residues and affine constants, with E,T,S,C_* fixed.
needed_assertion.constants: The Green-Tao divisor-sum construction provides a nonnegative normalized prime-cyclic majorant with any requested fixed finite pseudorandom complexity and domination of the appropriately rescaled prime weight, under its stated cutoff and size hypotheses.
needed_assertion.normalizations: Normalized cyclic averages; nu=(1+tilde-nu)/2 on [L], one outside; c_chi is retained; alpha=gamma/(8T c_chi), gamma=1/(32S).
needed_assertion.exceptional_cases: Historical DK and U^(2s)-only sufficiency are retired. Keep the correlation condition, repeated shifts, fixed-E primes and cutoff-dependent errors.
needed_assertion.limit_order: Fix E,T,S and the smoothing function first; ensure S covers (k+2)2^(k+1), then use a sufficiently slow z and let L grow.

assertion.statement: Place the current finite-complexity linear forms into normal form by adding averaging variables and preserving input projection.
assertion.objects: For each i!=j select fixed integer v_ij with dot(psi_j)(v_ij)=0 and dot(psi_i)(v_ij)!=0; substitute m=x+sum y_ij*v_ij.
assertion.hypotheses: All linear parts are nonzero, fixed, and pairwise nonproportional. New y variables range over a full box of side comparable to N/V_z. For t=1 choose v with dot(psi_1)(v)!=0. The extended convex region is defined by original constraints on x+Vy together with the full y box.
assertion.quantifiers: For every choice of the application parameters satisfying these hypotheses at the named current consumer; no conclusion is claimed for a different proof stage.
assertion.parameter_range: All linear parts are nonzero, fixed, and pairwise nonproportional. New y variables range over a full box of side comparable to N/V_z. For t=1 choose v with dot(psi_1)(v)!=0. The extended convex region is defined by original constraints on x+Vy together with the full y box.
assertion.uniformity: Each i has a block of active variables absent from each competing form. Apply normal-form GN, then divide by the added box cardinality.
assertion.constants: A finite-complexity system of nonzero pairwise nonproportional affine-linear forms can be extended to the stated normal form by adjoining variables and using the given invertible integer change of variables.
assertion.normalizations: The integer map (x,y)->(x+Vy,y) is bijective; the sum is multiplied by the exact box cardinality. No restriction to a zero section is used.
assertion.exceptional_cases: Use the full auxiliary box and its exact multiplicity; a zero-section restriction does not establish equivalence of averages.
assertion.limit_order: Fix the form system and its integer annihilating vectors before the ambient size and cutoff limits.

assertion.statement: Supply the ordinary-prime polynomial-pattern majorant with the fixed factor E and the required normalization.
assertion.objects: Ordinary polynomial majorant nu_b for W=E*primorial(v), fixed E, and unit b modulo W.
assertion.hypotheses: Unit residues exclude every divisor condition at primes dividing W, regardless of their exponents. Remaining local factors are unchanged; fixed E is absorbed into coefficient bounds. Choose small sieve exponent after all fixed polynomial complexities.
assertion.quantifiers: For every choice of the application parameters satisfying these hypotheses at the named current consumer; no conclusion is claimed for a different proof stage.
assertion.parameter_range: Unit residues exclude every divisor condition at primes dividing W, regardless of their exponents. Remaining local factors are unchanged; fixed E is absorbed into coefficient bounds. Choose small sieve exponent after all fixed polynomial complexities.
assertion.uniformity: Provides the model/GN majorants and the polynomial moments used for the boundary argument.
assertion.constants: The normalized ordinary-prime divisor-sum construction supplies the model and polynomial-forms majorant with the specified domination and moment estimates for a fixed family and sufficiently small sieve exponent.
assertion.normalizations: This is an explicit fixed-E adaptation of the source construction. Nu concerns ordinary primes and does not itself imply ray-prime equidistribution.
assertion.exceptional_cases: Unit residues eliminate primes dividing W even with powers in E; the remaining local factors are unchanged. This is not a ray-density theorem.
assertion.limit_order: Choose the sieve exponent after all polynomial complexities, then the cutoff, then size.

assertion.objects: H_j=gamma_j^(-1)*G-prime*gamma_j; Lambda_j=H_j intersect Gamma; h_j=gamma_j^(-1)*g-prime*gamma_j. F_jk(x Lambda_j)=F(a_jk*gamma_j*x Gamma).
assertion.hypotheses: Reduced gamma_j has rational coordinates of height M^O(1); a_jk=epsilon(n_jk) has bounded M-power coordinates. The output subgroup basis and lattice satisfy the published claim.
assertion.quantifiers: For every choice of the application parameters satisfying these hypotheses at the named current consumer; no conclusion is claimed for a different proof stage.
assertion.parameter_range: Reduced gamma_j has rational coordinates of height M^O(1); a_jk=epsilon(n_jk) has bounded M-power coordinates. The output subgroup basis and lattice satisfy the published claim.
assertion.uniformity: Obtain basis rationality M^C2, total M^(-aB+C2)-equidistribution and Lip norm M^C2. Account for commensurable lattices and finite-index losses; conjugation is not an isometry of the original quotients. Subtract each new quotient Haar mean, including the dimension-zero case. The claim is used for a general weight through separate mean/minor-arc hypotheses, not by extending the Möbius theorem.
assertion.constants: The published quantitative conjugation claim transfers a rational subgroup orbit to the conjugated quotient with the actual intersection lattice, controlling rationality, equidistribution and Lipschitz losses by fixed powers of the height bound.
assertion.normalizations: G connected, simply connected and nilpotent; Gamma discrete cocompact; filtration by closed connected rational subgroups; adapted rational Malcev basis; C-infinity norm in the binomial basis modulo one; Lipschitz norm includes supremum norm. Nontrivial horizontal characters are integer-lattice characters annihilating commutators and Gamma.
assertion.exceptional_cases: The quotient comparison is not an isometry; finite-index and Lipschitz losses and the zero-dimensional case remain explicit.
assertion.limit_order: Fix B and the resulting M, then permit fixed powers of M in the new basis, metric and equidistribution losses.

assertion.statement: Factor the current polynomial orbit into smooth, equidistributed and rational-periodic factors with the stated M bounds.
assertion.objects: Initial polynomial g on G/Gamma, M0=log(2N)^max(1,C_init), external exponent A renamed B; g=epsilon*g-prime*gamma.
assertion.hypotheses: Initial basis is log(2N)^C_init-rational, hence M0-rational; fixed dimension m, degree d. Output M0<=M<=C*M0^E(B), rational subgroup G-prime and Gamma-prime=G-prime intersect Gamma.
assertion.quantifiers: For every choice of the application parameters satisfying these hypotheses at the named current consumer; no conclusion is claimed for a different proof stage.
assertion.parameter_range: Initial basis is log(2N)^C_init-rational, hence M0-rational; fixed dimension m, degree d. Output M0<=M<=C*M0^E(B), rational subgroup G-prime and Gamma-prime=G-prime intersect Gamma.
assertion.uniformity: epsilon is (M,N)-smooth, g-prime totally M^(-B)-equidistributed, gamma rational with coset period q<=M. B is chosen using lower M>=log(2N) before E(B) is used for the later progression threshold; no circular comparison B>E(B).
assertion.constants: The quantitative polynomial-orbit factorization theorem gives g=epsilon g-prime gamma, where epsilon is (M,N)-smooth, g-prime is totally M^(-B)-equidistributed on a rational subgroup, and gamma has rational coset period at most M, for M between M0 and a fixed power of M0 depending on the chosen B.
assertion.normalizations: G connected, simply connected and nilpotent; Gamma discrete cocompact; filtration by closed connected rational subgroups; adapted rational Malcev basis; C-infinity norm in the binomial basis modulo one; Lipschitz norm includes supremum norm. Nontrivial horizontal characters are integer-lattice characters annihilating commutators and Gamma.
assertion.exceptional_cases: Do not require a circular inequality B>E(B); the lower logarithmic bound supplies the needed decay.
assertion.limit_order: Choose the desired equidistribution exponent B from the lower bound M>=M_0 before using the resulting E(B).

assertion.statement: From an actually bad product orbit in the type-II step obtain a nonzero character pair on the product nilmanifold.
assertion.objects: For many pairs r,r-prime, restrict n -> (g(rn),g(r-prime*n)) in (G/Gamma)^2 to a bad progression.
assertion.hypotheses: Use the product filtration, product lattice and concatenated adapted basis. Product orbit failure is obtained by contraposition of norm transfer; equidistribution of separate factors is never asserted to imply product equidistribution.
assertion.quantifiers: For every choice of the application parameters satisfying these hypotheses at the named current consumer; no conclusion is claimed for a different proof stage.
assertion.parameter_range: Use the product filtration, product lattice and concatenated adapted basis. Product orbit failure is obtained by contraposition of norm transfer; equidistribution of separate factors is never asserted to imply product equidistribution.
assertion.uniformity: Obtain a nonzero pair of horizontal characters, clear shift denominators and pigeonhole. Interchange coordinates if needed to ensure the first character is nonzero; fix one r-prime with many partners.
assertion.constants: The same one-parameter quantitative Leibman theorem applies to the product nilmanifold in dimension2m with its product filtration and concatenated rational basis. A nonzero horizontal character is a nonzero pair of factor characters.
assertion.normalizations: G connected, simply connected and nilpotent; Gamma discrete cocompact; filtration by closed connected rational subgroups; adapted rational Malcev basis; C-infinity norm in the binomial basis modulo one; Lipschitz norm includes supremum norm. Nontrivial horizontal characters are integer-lattice characters annihilating commutators and Gamma.
assertion.exceptional_cases: Bad product equidistribution is a premise supplied by the type-II argument, not inferred from separate factor failures.
assertion.limit_order: Use dimension 2m and the product filtration before recurrence and pigeonholing.

assertion.statement: Apply polynomial recurrence to the dense set of type-I phases d! beta_j r^j while preserving the short-arc factor.
assertion.objects: Polynomial r -> d!*beta_j*r^j modulo one on [ceil(R)] for each 1<=j<=d.
assertion.hypotheses: Selected r have eta-power density. Values lie in an arc of length <=2*eta^(-C5)*(R/N)^j. R<=2*N^(2/3), sufficiently large K_rec, and the large-R branch ensure arc length at most half density. Small R is treated internally by multiplying by r^d.
assertion.quantifiers: For every choice of the application parameters satisfying these hypotheses at the named current consumer; no conclusion is claimed for a different proof stage.
assertion.parameter_range: Selected r have eta-power density. Values lie in an arc of length <=2*eta^(-C5)*(R/N)^j. R<=2*N^(2/3), sufficiently large K_rec, and the large-R branch ensure arc length at most half density. Small R is treated internally by multiplying by r^d.
assertion.uniformity: Retain the arc-length factor in the published smoothness conclusion; the leading coefficient then has N^(-j), not merely R^(-j), accuracy. Additional factorial and product of nonzero bounded integers yield one character.
assertion.constants: If a polynomial phase takes values in a sufficiently short arc on a positive-density subset of an interval, the recurrence lemma gives a bounded nonzero integer multiple with a C-infinity bound retaining the arc-length factor and a power loss in the density.
assertion.normalizations: G connected, simply connected and nilpotent; Gamma discrete cocompact; filtration by closed connected rational subgroups; adapted rational Malcev basis; C-infinity norm in the binomial basis modulo one; Lipschitz norm includes supremum norm. assertion.exceptional_cases: The arc factor is needed to recover N^-j precision and cannot be discarded.
assertion.limit_order: Check that the arc is at most half the density in the large-R range; treat small R before applying recurrence.

assertion.uniformity: Metric comparison bounds the test Lip norm by T^C. Choose C*c0<1/4 and c0<1/4, then small sigma0 handles floors. The obstruction itself is proved internally; no external converse-equidistribution theorem is assumed.

assertion.statement: Obtain a nonzero horizontal character obstruction for each bad one-parameter quadratic row pullback.
assertion.objects: Apply to t -> g(P(t)) Gamma on [L], with P an integer quadratic from a horizontal Gaussian-norm row. Target discrepancy epsilon=delta^kappa; dimension m and filtration degree at most 2d.
assertion.hypotheses: Q<=delta^(-kappa)=epsilon^(-1); the stretched filtration and unchanged basis are supplied by V6-GN-COORDINATES. Failure of ordinary epsilon-equidistribution gives a nonzero horizontal character with epsilon-power size and smoothness bounds. L>=sqrt(X)/B0, B0<=delta^(-5kappa).
assertion.quantifiers: For every choice of the application parameters satisfying these hypotheses at the named current consumer; no conclusion is claimed for a different proof stage.
assertion.parameter_range: Q<=delta^(-kappa)=epsilon^(-1); the stretched filtration and unchanged basis are supplied by V6-GN-COORDINATES. Failure of ordinary epsilon-equidistribution gives a nonzero horizontal character with epsilon-power size and smoothness bounds. L>=sqrt(X)/B0, B0<=delta^(-5kappa).
assertion.uniformity: Internal integer coefficient extrapolation returns k*eta on the original orbit. Choose C_* first, then 6*C_*kappa<c0/2, sigma<sigma0 and 2*kappa*sigma<1/4. The internal horizontal-character obstruction contradicts total delta-equidistribution. Only ordinary distribution is deduced for each row pullback.
assertion.constants: For a one-parameter polynomial orbit on a rational filtered nilmanifold that fails ordinary epsilon-equidistribution, the quantitative Leibman theorem gives a nonzero horizontal character with epsilon-power bounds on its magnitude and binomial C-infinity smoothness norm.
assertion.normalizations: G connected, simply connected and nilpotent; Gamma discrete cocompact; filtration by closed connected rational subgroups; adapted rational Malcev basis; C-infinity norm in the binomial basis modulo one; Lipschitz norm includes supremum norm. Nontrivial horizontal characters are integer-lattice characters annihilating commutators and Gamma.
assertion.exceptional_cases: Only ordinary equidistribution of the row pullback is inferred; no multiparameter theorem is used.
assertion.limit_order: Fix the stretched degree and C_* before kappa and sigma; the small exponents are chosen before X.

assertion.statement: A nonconstant rational function on a nonempty rational affine open cannot take only integer values on its rational points.
assertion.objects: The composite of X1/X0 with the dominant rational parametrization of the actual quotient cubic.
assertion.hypotheses: The parametrization is dominant over Q; its domain meets the input chart in a nonempty open; X1/X0 is nonconstant.
assertion.quantifiers: For the exact current objects and each place or point quantified in the indicated argument.
assertion.parameter_range: Characteristic zero over Q; the actual cubic dimension>=2 branch where applicable.
assertion.uniformity: No quantitative parametrization or new uniformity assertion is introduced.
assertion.constants: No numerical constant is required.
assertion.normalizations: Shrink to a rational affine principal open avoiding the denominator. No density of rational points on the cubic itself is assumed.
assertion.exceptional_cases: Lower-dimensional branches and positive characteristic are outside this use.
assertion.limit_order: Dominance preserves nonconstancy in function fields. Choose a real ball in the affine principal open. Rational density and continuity put its whole image in the closed set Z; connectedness makes that image constant. The numerator minus this constant times the denominator vanishes on a real open ball, hence identically, contradiction.

assertion.statement: For the specified q0,q1 and J, J^2 q_i have nonnegative valuation at each vertical generic point of the maximal stack.
assertion.objects: The actual t=32s, four branch values a_i, q0=(dt)^2/product(t-a_i), q1=tq0, and J=product p^delta_p.
assertion.hypotheses: The maximal stack is semistable and regular; at a vertical generic point p is a uniformizer and the relative differential kills p. The displayed forms and delta_p use the fixed branch values.
assertion.quantifiers: For the exact current objects and each place or point quantified in the indicated argument.
assertion.parameter_range: The actual discriminant210 maximal stack and all vertical generic points.
assertion.uniformity: No quantitative parametrization or new uniformity assertion is introduced.
assertion.constants: The same J=2765952000 and delta_p; no new height constant.
assertion.normalizations: Work on the maximal stack, with ordinary p-adic valuations; no integral coarse pullback is used.
assertion.exceptional_cases: Codimension-two extension and archimedean metric comparison remain separate.
assertion.limit_order: Write r_i=v(t-a_i). Since d(p)=0, v(dt)>=max r_i. If v(t)<0 all r_i agree and both forms have nonnegative valuation. Otherwise at most one r_i exceeds delta_p and 2max r_i-sum r_i>=-2delta_p. Multiplication by J^2 cancels this possible pole. Extension across codimension2 is a distinct retained input, not a conclusion of this valuation calculation.

assertion.statement: The actual sections J^2 q_i, already regular at every codimension-one point, extend uniquely across codimension two on the maximal stack.
assertion.objects: The regular Noetherian maximal D210 Deligne-Mumford stack and its invertible square-dualizing line with rational sections J^2 q0,J^2 q1.
assertion.hypotheses: The stack is regular and flat over the base. The line is invertible, the sections are regular on the generic fibre, and the separately proved vertical valuation bounds give regularity at vertical codimension-one points.
assertion.quantifiers: Both displayed sections, on every regular etale chart and every codimension-one point.
assertion.parameter_range: The actual maximal stack, including primes dividing210; no tame coarse quotient is assumed there.
assertion.uniformity: The same rational sections and line extend; no rescaling beyond the already fixed J^2.
assertion.constants: J remains2765952000; no new height constant.
assertion.normalizations: Trivialize the line on affine regular etale charts; apply the source with M=R, a free rank-one and hence reflexive module.
assertion.exceptional_cases: This does not construct a coarse-model line bundle, supply the valuation bounds, or extend a general nonreflexive sheaf.
assertion.limit_order: Choose an etale scheme atlas of the regular Noetherian Deligne-Mumford maximal stack and trivialize the invertible square-dualizing line on affine open charts. Each connected regular chart is a normal domain. The generic bicanonical section is regular at horizontal height-one primes; the separate vertical valuation calculation proves it at vertical height-one primes. Apply Tag0AVB with the free rank-one module, which is reflexive, to obtain a unique regular section on each chart. The extensions agree on etale overlaps because they agree on the dense generic fibre and the line is locally free on a reduced flat atlas. Descent for sections gives the unique section on the stack. No coarse-model pullback or tame argument at bad primes is used.

assertion.hypotheses: The actual principal datum maps to this component through the separately supplied A001 coarse quotient. Retain the exact published intersection and divisor assertions as inputs.
assertion.quantifiers: The stated global identities and the specified CM(-4) and CM(-24) evaluations on this component.
assertion.parameter_range: Characteristic zero, same point and weight conventions. Evaluate ratios only when their denominators are nonzero.
assertion.uniformity: No other quaternionic discriminant or arbitrary polarization is covered.
assertion.constants: The exact constants in published equations13–14 and Examples29–30; no use of the CM(-19) value81/64.
assertion.normalizations: j(CM-4)=0, j(CM-3)=infinity, j(CM-24)=-16/27; Siegel weights4,6,10,12 and projective weights2,3,5,6; Igusa weights1,2,3,5.
assertion.exceptional_cases: Do not infer global ratio shapes from finite evaluations. Product intersection is principally polarized, not merely an isogeny. No BG explicit conic map or product-isomorphism proof is imported.
assertion.limit_order: First retain published global shapes and intersection inputs, then determine constants; subsequent weighted conversion and Q-definition keep their separate premises.
